guide.title: Steakhouses in London: Twenty-Eight Rooms Across Six Boroughs
guide.intro: Twenty-eight rooms, and fifteen of them are in Westminster alone — Mayfair, Soho, the Strand and Piccadilly hold the core of London's steak trade the way the City holds its banks. Four more sit inside the City of London itself, three in Tower Hamlets between Redchurch Street and Canary Wharf, two apiece in Camden, Southwark and Hackney. Nine of them are named on the 2026 World's 101 ranking of steak restaurants. What spreads the corpus is the multi-site operators: Hawksmoor keeps seven rooms on this page, from a former hops warehouse at Borough to a floating pavilion at Wood Wharf, Blacklock four chophouses, Gaucho two Argentine grills and Flat Iron two single-cut rooms. The rest are one-offs, and several of them are pubs with a grill upstairs.

sections.heading: Mayfair, Soho and the West End
sections.body:
Fifteen of the twenty-eight sit in the City of Westminster, and they are not one kind of room.

Goodman Mayfair is at 24-26 Maddox Street, and the operator calls it "the first Goodman, the flagship, 2008 original". Each Goodman keeps its own ageing room, where the kitchen dry ages the beef and cuts, trims and prepares it by hand; the daily specials board is called The Cut. The Guinea Grill is round the corner at 30 Bruton Place, in a Mayfair mews, with a Young's pub over the restaurant and a meat counter at the door. An inn has stood on the site since 1423, according to the restaurant's own history; the grill itself opened in 1952. The beef is dry-aged and grass-fed British, supplied by Godfreys of Finsbury Park and cooked over an open grill, and the beef shin, Guinness and oyster pie carries a suet lid.

CUT at 45 Park Lane is the Wolfgang Puck room, one of seven CUTs worldwide. Beast is at 3 Chapel Place off Oxford Street and serves two things — beef and crab — which is the whole proposition. Zoilo is on Duke Street, a modern Argentine grill.

Soho carries three. Blacklock Soho, at 24 Great Windmill Street, is the first of the group's chophouses; the operator says Blacklock "was born from a love of the traditional Chophouse", the trade of serving cuts of meat left on the bone for the flavour it adds. Sophie's Steakhouse is a few doors along at 42-44 Great Windmill Street, with the Jack Solomons cocktail bar attached, and Flat Iron Soho is at 17 Beak Street, where the menu is one cut and the cut is beef. The Devonshire is at 17 Denman Street: a pub downstairs, a grill room above it, a wood ember fire and Scottish beef dry-aged and butchered on site, with creel-caught langoustines from Oban and hand-dived Devon scallops beside it.

On the Strand and around Piccadilly: Smith & Wollensky occupies the Adelphi Building at 1-11 John Adam Street, the American chophouse's only British room, working USDA Prime dry-aged beef; STK London is at 336-337 Strand; Gaucho Piccadilly is at 25 Swallow Street; Hawksmoor Air Street is up an Art Deco staircase at 5a Air Street with ten commissioned floor-to-ceiling stained-glass windows over Regent Street; Blacklock Covent Garden is at 16a Bedford Street and Flat Iron Covent Garden at 17 Henrietta Street.

sections.heading: The City and the eastern boroughs
sections.body:
Nine rooms east of Kingsway, and the City's four are the densest quarter-mile on this page.

Goodman City is at 11 Old Jewry, a business-lunch room by day. Blacklock City is at 13 Philpot Lane. Lutyens Grill is the grill room inside The Ned at 27 Poultry. Hawksmoor Guildhall is at 10 Basinghall Street, a few minutes from the site of Dolly's, a chophouse the restaurant's own history dates to somewhere between 1702 and 1714; a newspaper of the mid-1800s praised its bars for "simmering and simpering forth their greaseful admiration of the tender steaks upon them".

Shoreditch straddles two boroughs and holds three rooms. Blacklock Shoreditch is at 28-30 Rivington Street and Sagardi at Cordy House, 95 Curtain Road, both in Hackney; Sagardi is a Basque asador run by the brothers Iñaki and Mikel López de Viñaspre, and its txuleta is the reason to go. Brat is on Redchurch Street in Tower Hamlets, cooking whole beef over fire, with a second kitchen at Climpson's Arch in Hackney.

Further east, Hawksmoor Wood Wharf is at 1 Water Street in Canary Wharf, an eco-designed floating pavilion that rises and falls with the tide and the group's largest London room, with a 120-seat waterside bar. Hawksmoor Spitalfields at 157a Commercial Street was the first of them all to open.

sections.heading: Camden and Southwark
sections.body:
Four rooms south and north of the centre.

Hawksmoor Borough is at 16 Winchester Walk, on the edge of Borough Market, in a former hops warehouse and auction hall — a building that was already in the meat and drink trade before the restaurant arrived. Gaucho Tower Bridge is at 2 More London Place, on the river walk between the bridge and City Hall; open-fire cooking has been the operator's method since 1994, according to Gaucho's own account of itself.

In Camden, Hawksmoor Seven Dials is at 11 Langley Street in what was the Watney-Combe brewery, once the largest brewer in London — and the restaurant found that its first owner, Alderman Combe, had hosted an annual steak supper, reported in 1807 as having left the company "highly gratified with their beef-steaks". Hawksmoor St Pancras is the newest of the seven, on Euston Road inside St Pancras station.

sections.heading: How the beef is worked
sections.body:
Three of the multi-site operators publish what they do to the beef, and the three answers are different.

Hawksmoor works native British breeds and puts Longhorn — the rare breed the group says helped shape it nearly twenty years ago — on the menu as sharing cuts of dry-aged beef cooked over live charcoal with roasted bone marrow and slow-cooked onions. The Michelin Guide's line on the Spitalfields room is that it is "all about British beef here: hand-butchered, hung for 35 days", according to the guide's 2023 entry.

Goodman gives every restaurant its own ageing room and dry ages in house, with the chefs cutting and trimming by hand each day. Blacklock does not run an ageing programme as its headline; it runs a chophouse, with big chops at butcher's prices on Mondays and a Sunday roast the rest of the week.

And then there is the opposite approach: Flat Iron sells one cut, priced flat, in two rooms on this page and fourteen more across London that this survey did not scope.

faq.question: Why twenty-eight rooms and not thirty-seven?
faq.answer: Because nine of the thirty-seven the scoping survey counted could not be stood up when each operator's own site was read at the time of writing. Goodman no longer lists a Canary Wharf room; Gaucho's own list of its eleven London restaurants contains neither Charlotte Street nor Smithfield; Sophie's lists Soho and no Chelsea room; Zelman Meats and M Restaurant Threadneedle Street could not be reached at all, so their trading status is unverified. Two names on the survey — Ibai and Chelsea Grill — carried no address and could not be located in London. Boisdale of Belgravia was set aside on the inclusion rule rather than on status: it describes itself as a British restaurant of Scottish flavours with dry-aged Aberdeenshire steaks, Hebridean seafood and haggis among its highlights, which is a good steak on a broad menu rather than a steakhouse.

faq.question: What makes a room a steakhouse on this page?
faq.answer: Steak has to be the menu's centre of gravity, plus the beef-centric genres — churrascaria, Argentine parrilla, Japanese wagyu counter, Korean-style beef room. In London that admits a Basque asador at Sagardi, two Argentine grills at Gaucho and Zoilo, a surf-and-turf room at Beast that serves beef and crab and nothing else, and two pubs, the Guinea Grill and the Devonshire, whose upstairs rooms are grills. It excludes a restaurant with a famous steak on an otherwise broad menu, however good the steak is.

faq.question: Does Hawksmoor really have seven rooms here?
faq.answer: Seven on this page, eight in the city. The operator's own list adds a Knightsbridge restaurant to the seven published here — Spitalfields, Seven Dials, St Pancras, Borough, Guildhall, Air Street and Wood Wharf. The scoping survey this page follows named seven, and the page does not widen a list the survey settled; Knightsbridge is noted here instead. Blacklock is the same shape: five London rooms on the operator's list, four scoped and published, with Canary Wharf at 5 Frobisher Passage the fifth.

faq.question: Which boroughs do the rooms sit in?
faq.answer: Six. Westminster carries fifteen, across Mayfair, Soho, the Strand and Piccadilly. The City of London carries four, all within a few streets of Bank. Tower Hamlets carries three — Spitalfields, Redchurch Street and Canary Wharf. Camden, Southwark and Hackney carry two each. Every room is filed under the most specific place it can be pinned to — Mayfair, Soho, Covent Garden, the Strand, Marylebone, Bank, Monument, Guildhall, Spitalfields, Canary Wharf, Shoreditch, Borough, London Bridge or King's Cross. Four stand on a boundary and stay at borough level: Air Street, Swallow Street, Langley Street and Redchurch Street.

faq.question: What about the 2026 ranking?
faq.answer: Nine of the rooms the scoping survey counted are named on the 2026 World's 101 ranking of steak restaurants. This page states that membership and does not print a placing for any individual room, because two of the nine — Ibai and Chelsea Grill — could not be located in London at all, which is reason enough not to assert the rest of that column room by room.

faq.question: Why is Flat Iron only two rooms?
faq.answer: Because that is what the scoping survey counted. Flat Iron's own London list runs to sixteen restaurants, from Borough and Kings Cross to Westfield and Waterloo. The two published here, Covent Garden at 17 Henrietta Street and Soho at 17 Beak Street, are the two the survey named, and the page does not add rooms the survey did not reach.

photos.title: Bruton Place, Mayfair, London
photos.description: A narrow Mayfair mews under a clear blue sky, lined on the right by three-storey red and yellow brick buildings with white-framed sash and metal windows and small shopfronts at street level, some with clipped bay trees in planters outside. Double yellow lines run down both kerbs, a black Victorian lamp post stands at the left, and a white van and a few figures are parked and walking at the far end.
photos.author: Chris Whippet

places.name: Hawksmoor Spitalfields
places.summary: Hawksmoor's Spitalfields steak restaurant at 157a Commercial Street was the first of the group's rooms to open, and the operator still calls it the one that most embodies the house spirit. The Michelin Guide's 2023 entry describes it as all about British beef, hand-butchered and hung for 35 days, according to the guide.

places.name: Hawksmoor Seven Dials
places.summary: The Seven Dials steak restaurant occupies the old Watney-Combe brewery at 11 Langley Street in Covent Garden. Its first owner, Alderman Combe, hosted an annual steak supper there, and a newspaper report of 1807 has the company leaving "highly gratified with their beef-steaks", according to the restaurant's own history of the building.

places.name: Hawksmoor St Pancras
places.address: St Pancras London, Euston Road, London NW1 2AR
places.summary: The newest of Hawksmoor's seven London steak restaurants, on Euston Road inside St Pancras station, with a martini bar alongside the dining room.

places.name: Hawksmoor Borough
places.summary: Hawksmoor's Borough steak restaurant is at 16 Winchester Walk on the edge of Borough Market, in a former hops warehouse and auction hall. Dry-aged British beef over live charcoal is the house method here as at every Hawksmoor room.

places.name: Hawksmoor Guildhall
places.summary: The Guildhall steak restaurant is at 10 Basinghall Street, a short walk from Bank and from the site of Dolly's, a chophouse the restaurant's own history places as opening somewhere between 1702 and 1714. Available steaks are chalked up on a board for the room to claim.

places.name: Hawksmoor Air Street
places.summary: Hawksmoor Air Street is a sweeping Art Deco room over Regent Street, near Piccadilly Circus, lit by ten specially commissioned floor-to-ceiling stained-glass windows. The menu is weighted evenly between steak and sustainable seafood, and it is where the group's seafood cooking began.

places.name: Hawksmoor Wood Wharf
places.summary: The Canary Wharf steak restaurant sits in an eco-designed floating pavilion at 1 Water Street that rises and falls with the tide. It is the group's largest London room, with a 120-seat waterside bar joined to the restaurant above it and a terrace over the dock.

places.name: Goodman Mayfair
places.summary: Goodman's Maddox Street room is the group's flagship and its 2008 original. Every Goodman keeps its own ageing room, where the beef is dry aged and then cut, trimmed and prepared by hand for the daily specials board the house calls The Cut.

places.name: Goodman City
places.summary: The City branch of Goodman is at 11 Old Jewry, a lunch and dinner steak room for the Square Mile that regulars describe to the operator as a clubhouse. Like its Mayfair sibling it has its own ageing room and dry ages the beef in house.

places.name: Blacklock Soho
places.summary: The first Blacklock, at 24 Great Windmill Street in Soho. The group says it was born from a love of the traditional chophouse — cuts of meat left attached to the bone for the flavour it adds — and it runs big chops at butcher's prices on Mondays and a roast on Sundays.

places.name: Blacklock City
places.summary: Blacklock's City chophouse is at 13 Philpot Lane, a few streets from Monument. Chops and steaks off the bone are the menu, with the group's Sunday roast and its Monday butcher's-price chops running as they do at every Blacklock.

places.name: Blacklock Shoreditch
places.summary: The Shoreditch chophouse at 28-30 Rivington Street, in Hackney. Blacklock's whole proposition is the chophouse revived: cuts of meat on the bone, cooked over coals, at butcher's prices on a Monday.

places.name: Blacklock Covent Garden
places.summary: Blacklock's Covent Garden room is at 16a Bedford Street, off the Strand. Chops and steaks are the whole card, and it takes pre- and post-theatre sittings the other branches do not need to.

places.name: Gaucho Piccadilly
places.summary: Gaucho's Swallow Street parrilla, off Piccadilly, is one of eleven Argentine steak restaurants the operator runs across London. Beef over open fire has been the group's method since 1994, according to Gaucho's own account of itself.

places.name: Gaucho Tower Bridge
places.summary: The Tower Bridge parrilla sits at 2 More London Place, on the south bank walk between the bridge and City Hall. Argentine beef over open fire is the house method here as at every Gaucho.

places.name: Flat Iron Covent Garden
places.summary: Flat Iron's Covent Garden room at 17 Henrietta Street sells one cut of beef at one price, which is the group's entire idea. It is one of sixteen Flat Iron restaurants across London.

places.name: Flat Iron Soho
places.summary: The Beak Street room in Soho, where the menu is a single steak and the group's strapline is great steak for everyone. One cut, and the cut is beef.

places.name: Beast
places.summary: Beast is down a doorway at 3 Chapel Place, off Oxford Street, and it serves two things: beef and king crab. Communal tables, evenings only from Monday to Wednesday and lunch as well from Thursday to Saturday, per the restaurant's own opening hours, and a surf-and-turf format the operator has run for ten years.

places.name: Smith & Wollensky London
places.address: The Adelphi Building, 1-11 John Adam Street, London WC2N 6HT
places.summary: The American steakhouse's only British room occupies the Adelphi Building at 1-11 John Adam Street, on the Covent Garden riverside just off the Strand. USDA Prime dry-aged steaks are the programme, with seafood brought from the coast daily.

places.name: Sophie's Steakhouse
places.summary: Sophie's Steakhouse and Cocktail Bar is at 42-44 Great Windmill Street in Soho, with the Jack Solomons Club attached for drinks. It is the operator's only remaining room.

places.name: CUT at 45 Park Lane
places.summary: Wolfgang Puck's London steakhouse occupies the ground floor of the 45 Park Lane hotel in Mayfair, one of seven CUT restaurants worldwide alongside Beverly Hills, Las Vegas, New York, Washington, Bahrain and Singapore.

places.name: STK London
places.summary: STK's Strand steakhouse is one of the group's two London rooms, the other being at Celebration Avenue in Stratford. New York strip and wagyu carry the beef list, in a dining room run more like a lounge.

places.name: The Guinea Grill
places.summary: The Guinea Grill sits behind a Young's pub in a Mayfair mews at 30 Bruton Place, with a meat counter at the entrance and dry-aged grass-fed British beef cooked over an open grill. An inn has stood on the site since 1423, according to the restaurant's own history, and the grill room itself opened in 1952.
places.history: The beef comes from Godfreys of Finsbury Park, a family butcher, and arrives daily for the counter by the door. The kitchen has put suet-lidded pies on the menu since the 1940s, per its own account, and the signature is a beef shin, Guinness and oyster pie topped with a deep-fried oyster.

places.name: Lutyens Grill
places.summary: Lutyens Grill is the steakhouse inside The Ned at 27 Poultry, in the heart of the City of London. It is a grill room rather than a hotel dining room, and it is one of the several restaurants the building holds.

places.name: The Devonshire
places.summary: The Devonshire is a pub at 17 Denman Street in Soho with a restaurant and grill room above it, working a wood ember grill. The beef is Scottish, dry-aged and butchered on site, and the kitchen runs its own butcher and bakery.

places.name: Brat
places.summary: Brat is up a staircase on Redchurch Street in Shoreditch and cooks whole beef over fire. A second Brat kitchen runs at Climpson's Arch in Hackney.

places.name: Sagardi
places.address: Cordy House, 95 Curtain Road, London EC2A 3BS
places.summary: Sagardi is a Basque grill at Cordy House on Curtain Road in Shoreditch, run by the brothers Iñaki and Mikel López de Viñaspre. The txuleta — the aged Basque beef chop — is the dish the room is built around.

places.name: Zoilo
places.summary: Zoilo is a modern Argentine grill on Duke Street, a short walk from Selfridges, working regional Argentine cooking around the beef rather than a straight parrilla format.

entries.name: Hawksmoor Spitalfields
entries.note: 157a Commercial Street, Tower Hamlets. The first Hawksmoor, and the one the staff send you to.

entries.name: Hawksmoor Seven Dials
entries.note: 11 Langley Street, Camden. An old brewery, and Sunday lunch is the sitting to book.

entries.name: Hawksmoor St Pancras
entries.note: Euston Road, inside the station. The one to use if you are catching a Eurostar.

entries.name: Hawksmoor Borough
entries.note: 16 Winchester Walk, Southwark. A hops warehouse before it was a steak restaurant, and it still reads like one.

entries.name: Hawksmoor Guildhall
entries.note: 10 Basinghall Street, City of London. Weekday lunches are business; Sundays have become the roast.

entries.name: Hawksmoor Air Street
entries.note: 5a Air Street, Westminster. Ten stained-glass windows over Regent Street, and the seafood half is real.

entries.name: Hawksmoor Wood Wharf
entries.note: 1 Water Street, Canary Wharf. The floor moves with the tide; the bar seats a hundred and twenty.

entries.name: Goodman Mayfair
entries.note: 24-26 Maddox Street. Ask what is on The Cut board before you look at the printed list.

entries.name: Goodman City
entries.note: 11 Old Jewry, by Bank. Closed Sundays, which tells you who it feeds.

entries.name: Blacklock Soho
entries.note: 24 Great Windmill Street. Monday lunch is the cheapest way into a big chop in central London.

entries.name: Blacklock City
entries.note: 13 Philpot Lane, near Monument. One of the four rooms on this page inside the City of London.

entries.name: Blacklock Shoreditch
entries.note: 28-30 Rivington Street, Hackney. Chops on the bone, coals, and not much else.

entries.name: Blacklock Covent Garden
entries.note: 16a Bedford Street. Book the pre-theatre sitting and you will make an eight o'clock curtain.

entries.name: Gaucho Piccadilly
entries.note: 25 Swallow Street, Westminster. The Argentine cuts are the point; the wine list is Argentine too.

entries.name: Gaucho Tower Bridge
entries.note: 2 More London Place, Southwark. Tables face the river and the bridge.

entries.name: Flat Iron Covent Garden
entries.note: 17 Henrietta Street. One cut, one price, no reservations — turn up early.

entries.name: Flat Iron Soho
entries.note: 17 Beak Street. The same single steak as Henrietta Street, in a smaller room.

entries.name: Beast
entries.note: 3 Chapel Place, off Oxford Street. Beef and king crab, communal tables, and no third option.

entries.name: Smith & Wollensky London
entries.note: The Adelphi Building, just off the Strand. The American chophouse's only room in Britain.

entries.name: Sophie's Steakhouse
entries.note: 42-44 Great Windmill Street. Late kitchen hours, and the cocktail bar next door runs later still.

entries.name: CUT at 45 Park Lane
entries.note: 45 Park Lane, Mayfair. The hotel steakhouse on this page, and priced like one.

entries.name: STK London
entries.note: 336-337 Strand. A steakhouse run as a lounge; the Stratford room is the group's other London site.

entries.name: The Guinea Grill
entries.note: 30 Bruton Place, Mayfair. Order the pie as well as the steak; both come off the same beef.

entries.name: Lutyens Grill
entries.note: The Ned, 27 Poultry. The grill room among the several restaurants the building holds.

entries.name: The Devonshire
entries.note: 17 Denman Street, Soho. Drink downstairs, eat off the ember grill upstairs.

entries.name: Brat
entries.note: 4 Redchurch Street. Whole beef over fire, and the turbot if there are two of you.

entries.name: Sagardi
entries.note: 95 Curtain Road, Hackney. Basque txuleta, cooked the way an asador cooks it.

entries.name: Zoilo
entries.note: 9 Duke Street, Westminster. Argentine cooking by region rather than by cut.
